alignments.note: Subject and supplied object pronoun are helpers on the verb (rules 7, 9).
Nominalizing article of the articular infinitive; no preposition governs it, so no English word answers to it (rule 61).
Supplied temporal relativizer is a helper on the participle (rule 7).

Discontinuous under rule 15: the complementizer that introduces the infinitive's English clause rides with the infinitive, since no preposition governs the construction (rules 61, 40); subject and modal are helpers (rules 7, 9). Head on the meaning-bearing complement of the support-verb rendering show courage (rule 17).
Case preposition rides with the article on the English determiner (rule 21).
Dative relative rendered by the portmanteau wherewith, which carries the case in -with.
Infinitival to and copula are helpers; head on the lexical predicate bold (rules 7, 17).
Attributive article governing an expressed head noun (tinas) before a participle; the relativizer is the participle's helper (rules 31, 23).
Supplied relativizer is a helper on the participle (rule 31).
Source pronoun rendered of + pronoun; head on the pronoun (rule 17).
The comparative particle licenses the supplied if as a helper (rules 7, 11), no other source token being present to take it, as hos -> 'as though' at REV.5.6 and REV.13.3.
Discontinuous under rule 15; supplied subject pronoun is a helper on the participle (rule 7).
Greek is anarthrous, so the supplied determiner is a helper on the noun (rule 51).
